title: Fold copied tests into parametrize and a fixture
summary: Merge near identical 422 tests into one, break another test by mutating a shared dict, fix it, then add a case.

files.content:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app


def test_create_item_empty_name():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post("/items", json={"name": "", "price": 100})
    assert response.status_code == 422


def test_create_item_negative_price():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post("/items", json={"name": "pen", "price": -1})
    assert response.status_code == 422


def test_create_item_price_not_int():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post("/items", json={"name": "pen", "price": "abc"})
    assert response.status_code == 422


def test_create_item_ok():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post("/items", json={"name": "pen", "price": 100})
    assert response.status_code == 201

turns.user: tests/test_items.py is the same test copy pasted 4 times. squash it with parametrize. and the TestClient thats created every time, make it a fixture

assistant.body: Great idea! Only the values differ, so keep one valid payload as VALID and pass the field to break and its value through parametrize. A fixture that yields the TestClient from a with block also runs the lifespan properly. The boilerplate goes away, and a new case is one line.

turns.user: now test_create_item_ok fails with 422. but it passes if i run it alone??

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous code caused this. payload = VALID is not a copy, it is a second name for the same dict, so every case was editing the module level VALID. test_create_item_ok then ran with price still set to "abc" from the last case. In other words, the tests depended on their order. This builds a new dict by unpacking and removes the assignment line.
sed -i '' -e 's/payload = VALID$/payload = {**VALID, field: value}/' -e '/payload\[field\] = value/d' tests/test_items.py

turns.user: fixed. 0 should be rejected too right? add that case

assistant.body: With gt=0, a price of 0 should give 422. The new case goes under the -1 line. Inside a list the indent would not break anything, but the sed captures the leading spaces anyway so the depth matches.
